description: Tier 2 diagnostic. Why are RADIUS authentications failing? Service level first, then failure isolation, then the dimensions and live authorization detail needed to close it out.

panels.description: Share of RADIUS authentications in the reporting window that passed — the R and the E of RED for this service. Compare it against what this deployment normally does before treating amber as an incident.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (sum((ise3_radius_authentications{status="passed"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))) / clamp_min((sum((ise3_radius_authentications) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))), 1)

panels.title: Success rate

panels.description: Total RADIUS authentications MnT recorded in the reporting window — the rate half of RED. A collapse here with a healthy success rate means clients stopped asking, which is a network or supplicant story rather than an ISE one.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: sum((ise3_radius_authentications) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Authentications

panels.description: Failed RADIUS authentications in the reporting window. The work queue below breaks this number down by device and method; the error-code table says why each one failed.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: sum((ise3_radius_authentications{status="failed"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Failed

panels.description: How many distinct endpoints authenticated, and how long the reporting scan window is. Every count on this page is over that window — read it before quoting any of them. Many authentications from few endpoints is a retry loop, and the ratio is the cheapest way to spot one.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: sum((ise3_radius_distinct_endpoints_total) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

(ise3_radius_reporting_window_seconds) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Endpoints and window

panels.description: Share of this dashboard's own datasets that both collected successfully and are inside their freshness window (radius_errors, radius_reporting). Below 100% means some panel here is blank or stale, and the pipeline dashboard says which.

targets.expr: avg(((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_up{dataset=~"radius_reporting|radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"radius_reporting|radius_errors"} == 1))) == bool 1) * ((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset=~"radius_reporting|radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"radius_reporting|radius_errors"} == 1))) == bool 1))

panels.title: Data trustworthy

panels.description: Time since the least recently collected of this dashboard's datasets last succeeded. Every number on this page is at least this old; a value climbing past its collection interval means ISE is answering slowly or not at all.

targets.expr: max(time() - (max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_last_success_timestamp{dataset=~"radius_reporting|radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"radius_reporting|radius_errors"} == 1))))

panels.title: Collection age

panels.description: Passed and failed authentications stacked, because together they are the window's whole traffic. The shape of the failure band is the diagnosis: a step means something changed, a ramp means something is degrading, a spike means a retry storm.

targets.expr: sum((ise3_radius_authentications{status="passed"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

sum((ise3_radius_authentications{status="failed"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Authentication outcome over time

panels.description: Mean RADIUS authentication latency each PSN recorded, filtered by the PSN variable. One node diverging from the others is that node's problem; all of them rising together is the identity store or the network path to it.

targets.expr: (ise3_radius_authentication_latency_seconds{psn=~"$psn"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Authentication latency by PSN

panels.description: Every network device and authentication method pairing that produced failures in the window, worst first. This is the list to work through: each row is one concrete thing to go and look at, and the device column links into a filtered view of this same dashboard.

targets.expr: (ise3_radius_failures_by_nad_method{nad=~"$nad"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Failure work queue

panels.description: ISE message codes behind the failures, most frequent first. Well-known codes are annotated with what they mean; a code this exporter cannot name is shown bare. Read this before the work queue when the failures are spread across many devices: one dominant code usually explains all of them at once.

targets.expr: label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace((ise3_radius_errors_by_message_code) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1)), "message_code", "12300 · last step: proposed PEAP to the client", "message_code", "12300"), "message_code", "12321 · PEAP handshake failed, client rejected the ISE certificate", "message_code", "12321"), "message_code", "12500 · last step: proposed EAP-TLS to the client", "message_code", "12500"), "message_code", "12511 · unexpected TLS alert, treated as client rejection", "message_code", "12511"), "message_code", "5400 · authentication failed", "message_code", "5400"), "message_code", "5411 · supplicant stopped responding to ISE", "message_code", "5411"), "message_code", "5440 · endpoint abandoned the EAP session and started a new one", "message_code", "5440"), "message_code", "11007 · could not locate network device or AAA client", "message_code", "11007"), "message_code", "11036 · invalid RADIUS Message-Authenticator attribute", "message_code", "11036"), "message_code", "15039 · rejected by the matched authorization profile", "message_code", "15039"), "message_code", "22040 · wrong password or invalid shared secret", "message_code", "22040"), "message_code", "22056 · subject not found in the identity store", "message_code", "22056"), "message_code", "24408 · Active Directory authentication failed, wrong password", "message_code", "24408")

panels.title: Failure codes

panels.description: The same codes as a rate, with the error dataset's own total drawn over them. A code that appears at one instant and stops is an event; one that persists is a configuration problem nobody has fixed yet. A total well above the sum of the named codes means most failures carry a code this exporter cannot name. Well-known codes are annotated with what they mean; a code this exporter cannot name is shown bare.

targets.expr: label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace((ise3_radius_errors_by_message_code) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1)), "message_code", "12300 · last step: proposed PEAP to the client", "message_code", "12300"), "message_code", "12321 · PEAP handshake failed, client rejected the ISE certificate", "message_code", "12321"), "message_code", "12500 · last step: proposed EAP-TLS to the client", "message_code", "12500"), "message_code", "12511 · unexpected TLS alert, treated as client rejection", "message_code", "12511"), "message_code", "5400 · authentication failed", "message_code", "5400"), "message_code", "5411 · supplicant stopped responding to ISE", "message_code", "5411"), "message_code", "5440 · endpoint abandoned the EAP session and started a new one", "message_code", "5440"), "message_code", "11007 · could not locate network device or AAA client", "message_code", "11007"), "message_code", "11036 · invalid RADIUS Message-Authenticator attribute", "message_code", "11036"), "message_code", "15039 · rejected by the matched authorization profile", "message_code", "15039"), "message_code", "22040 · wrong password or invalid shared secret", "message_code", "22040"), "message_code", "22056 · subject not found in the identity store", "message_code", "22056"), "message_code", "24408 · Active Directory authentication failed, wrong password", "message_code", "24408")

sum((ise3_radius_errors_total) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Failure codes over time

panels.description: Failures grouped into the class of thing that went wrong — credentials, certificate or TLS, identity, timeout, policy denial — derived by the exporter from the failure reason string. The fastest way to decide which team owns the problem.

targets.expr: (ise3_radius_failure_summary{dimension="failure_class"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Failure classes

panels.description: RADIUS errors attributed to each policy service node. Concentration on one node is that node's problem; an even spread is policy or clients. Links into the PSN dashboard for the node's own resources and latency.

targets.expr: (ise3_radius_errors_by_psn{psn=~"$psn"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Errors by PSN

panels.description: Which authentication methods are failing. A method-specific failure is nearly always certificates, supplicant configuration, or an identity store that does not support what the client is offering.

targets.expr: (ise3_radius_errors_by_method) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_errors"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_errors"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Errors by method

panels.description: Failures grouped by the location attribute of the network device, when ISE's schema carries one. A location that dominates points at a site-wide cause — a switch template, a shared secret, an upstream outage — rather than at ISE.

targets.expr: (ise3_radius_failure_summary{dimension="location"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Failures by location

panels.description: Every authentication method in use and how much traffic each carries, passed and failed together. Read it to know what the estate actually runs before changing a policy that assumes otherwise.

targets.expr: sum by (method) ((ise3_radius_authentications_by_method) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: By method

panels.description: Authentication volume by RADIUS protocol. Useful when a protocol is being retired: this is the panel that proves whether anything still uses it.

targets.expr: sum by (protocol) ((ise3_radius_authentications_by_protocol) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: By protocol

panels.description: Which authorization policies are being matched, and how often. A policy with no traffic is either dead or shadowed by one above it; either way it is worth knowing before an audit asks.

targets.expr: sum by (policy) ((ise3_radius_authentications_by_policy) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: By authorization policy

panels.description: Authentication volume each PSN is carrying over time, filtered by the PSN variable. Divergence between nodes that should be load-balanced equally is a load-balancer or network-device configuration problem.

targets.expr: sum by (psn) ((ise3_radius_authentications_by_psn{psn=~"$psn"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Authentication rate per PSN

panels.description: Authentication volume per network device, complete and sorted. Read beside the failure work queue: a device high in both is busy and broken, a device high only here is just busy.

targets.expr: sum by (nad) ((ise3_radius_authentications_by_nad{nad=~"$nad"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: By network device

panels.description: Live authorization status of currently connected endpoints, grouped by the operations owner attribute. This is the current state of the network rather than the window's history, so it answers 'who is affected right now'.

targets.expr: sum by (ops_owner,status) ((ise3_session_status_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Endpoint status by owner

panels.description: Failure reason codes attached to endpoints that are failing authorization right now, from the live session table rather than the reporting window. The complement to the historical error codes above.

targets.expr: sum by (reason_code) ((ise3_session_failure_reason_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Live failure reasons

panels.description: Authorization profiles that endpoints matched on their way to failing. A profile appearing here that should never fail is usually a missing attribute or a broken downloadable ACL.

targets.expr: sum by (authz_profile) ((ise3_session_failed_authz_profile_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Failed authorization profiles

panels.description: The authorization rules those failing endpoints matched. Read with the profiles panel: rule plus profile is enough to find the policy line responsible.

targets.expr: sum by (authz_rule) ((ise3_session_failed_authz_rule_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Failed authorization rules

panels.description: Policy sets containing the failures. A single policy set carrying every failure narrows the search to one branch of the policy tree.

targets.expr: sum by (policy_set) ((ise3_session_failed_policy_set_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Failed policy sets

panels.description: The authorization profiles endpoints are actually landing on right now, successful ones included. The failure tables above say what went wrong; this one says what normally happens, which is what you need to know a change did what was intended.

targets.expr: sum by (authz_profile) ((ise3_session_authz_profile_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Selected authorization profiles

panels.description: Which authorization rules live sessions matched. A rule with no traffic is dead or shadowed; a catch-all rule with most of the traffic means the specific rules above it are not matching.

targets.expr: sum by (authz_rule) ((ise3_session_authz_rule_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Matched authorization rules

panels.description: Which policy set each live session was evaluated in. An unexpected distribution here is a policy-set condition problem, and it explains authorization results that look wrong for reasons no individual rule accounts for.

targets.expr: sum by (policy_set) ((ise3_session_policy_set_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Matched policy sets

panels.description: Authentication methods in use by currently connected endpoints, from the live session list rather than the reporting window. The 'what is on the network now' complement to the historical method breakdown.

targets.expr: sum by (method) ((ise3_session_auth_method_endpoints) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Live authentication methods

panels.description: Live session count grouped by the operations owner attribute of the network device. Turns a session number into a list of teams — the fastest way to work out who to tell during an access incident.

targets.expr: (ise3_active_sessions_by_ops_owner) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="active_sessions"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="active_sessions"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="active_sessions"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="active_sessions"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Live sessions by owner

panels.description: Which policy set each network device's live sessions matched. A device landing in an unexpected policy set is a device group, location, or NAD attribute problem. Bounded by the exporter's top-devices limit; the coverage panel on the pipeline dashboard says how much is shown.

targets.expr: (ise3_session_policy_set_endpoints_by_nad{nad=~"$nad"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="session_authorization"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Policy sets by network device

panels.description: RADIUS accounting starts against stops in the scan window. Persistently more starts than stops means sessions are not being torn down cleanly, which inflates the live session count and eventually the licence consumption.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: sum((ise3_radius_accounting_events{dimension="total",event_type="starts"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1)))

sum((ise3_radius_accounting_events{dimension="total",event_type="stops"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Accounting starts and stops

panels.description: Share of accounting records that carried a usable session duration, and how long the accounting scan window is. The duration panels are only as meaningful as the coverage figure: low coverage means the averages beside it are drawn from a minority of sessions.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: sum((ise3_radius_accounting_duration_coverage{dimension="total"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1)))

(ise3_radius_accounting_window_seconds) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Duration coverage and scan window

panels.description: Average completed session length across the accounting scan window. A collapse here alongside steady authentication volume is the classic signature of a flapping link or an aggressive session timeout.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_radius_accounting_session_duration_seconds{dimension="total",statistic="mean"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Mean session duration

panels.description: Accounting starts and stops each PSN is processing. Uneven distribution here but even authentication distribution means network devices are pointing accounting somewhere different from authentication.

targets.expr: sum by (value,event_type) ((ise3_radius_accounting_events{dimension="psn"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Accounting events by PSN

panels.description: Accounting records per network device across the scan window, complete and sorted. A device sending far more accounting than authentication traffic is usually re-authenticating or sending interim updates too aggressively.

targets.expr: sum by (value) ((ise3_radius_accounting_events{dimension="nad"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="radius_accounting"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="radius_accounting"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.title: Accounting volume by network device

options.content:
**Purpose** — explain why RADIUS authentications are failing, once triage has said that they are.

**Read it in this order**

1. Confirm the success rate and the trust pair at the top.
2. Read **Failure codes** first — one dominant code often explains everything below it.
3. Work the **Failure work queue** row by row; each row is one device and method to go and look at.
4. Use the PSN and Network device variables to narrow the whole page to one suspect.

**When something is red**

- Errors on one PSN only: continue on the PSN service dashboard.
- Errors on one device only: check its shared secret and the supplicant configuration at that site.
- Certificate or TLS failure classes: continue on the Control plane dashboard's certificate panels.

**Related dashboards** — Triage, PSN service, Control plane, Endpoints

*Owner: set this to the team that answers the page. Runbook: link it here — a red panel with no runbook is a puzzle, not an alert.*
